title: 2026 AMC 8 Problem 21
statement: Charlotte the spider is walking along a web shaped like a \(5\)-pointed star, shown in the figure below. The web has \(5\) outer points and \(5\) inner points. Each time Charlotte reaches a point, she randomly chooses a neighboring point and moves to that point. Charlotte starts at one of the outer points and makes \(3\) moves (re-visiting points is allowed). What is the probability she is now at one of the outer points of the star?

solutions.text: From an outer point, Charlotte must move to an inner point. From an inner point, \(2\) of the \(4\) neighboring points are outer, so the probability of moving to an outer point is \(\frac{1}{2}\). After one move she is inner. After two moves she is outer with probability \(\frac{1}{2}\) and inner with probability \(\frac{1}{2}\). After the third move, only the inner case can move to outer, with probability \(\frac{1}{2}\), so the final probability is \(\frac12\cdot\frac12=\frac14\).
hints: Track only outer versus inner points
From an inner point, half of the neighboring points are outer
